matchups.recap:
The Chair Force rolled out Trevor Lawrence for 26.1 and Trey McBride for 20.0, got a jolt from Jeremiyah Love at 12.0, and still couldn't get out of his own way. George Pickens turned in a stunned naval battle queen effort at 4.3, and J.K. Dobbins ate his trail cheese and salami all afternoon for a measly 3.6. That's the kind of Canoe Hike that turns a boss stat line into a Beak final score.

Lone Eagle didn't need style points, just Justin Jefferson going for 27.2 and Lamar Jackson putting up 24.96 like it was nothing, with Aaron Jones Sr. chipping in a boss 10.0. The game plan had a real feel for the matchup all day, and when Catalina Wine Mixon clawed back late, Lone Eagle had just enough cushion to survive it. Final margin of 5.96 means this one goes down as a proper Bust Hike, sticky buns on Sunday morning included.

away.name: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare

matchups.recap:
Harley Jarvis got his Swimming Basic in a 143.02 party that left Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare face down in the alpine vegetation. Ashton Jeanty went woodsman running to the camp store all afternoon on his way to 29.7, David Montgomery chipped in 27.4, and Jalen Hurts tacked on 24.72 like it was nothing. Even Tony Pollard's 3.9 stinker and Ja'Marr Chase's ghostly 2.2 couldn't dent this thing. Blue Ridge had the game plan and the firepower both, and honestly, I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF after a margin like that.

Meanwhile the Pill Pusher never found the trailhead, Bushwhacking without a compass from kickoff to final whistle. Chris Olave's 23.2 and Jared Goff's 16.44 were the only signs of life, while Drake London's 4.5 and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s 3.8 gonna need to patch those holes with more leaves, because this team got soaking wet. Chase Brown himself managed 16.3, ate quietly, and watched 85.34 total points get buried under a 57-point avalanche.

Funk that Junk squeaked out a Canoeing Masters-adjacent win, though at 4.06 they'll have to settle for just calling it a Boss escape. Jaxon Smith-Njigba went off for 22.2, the Steelers D/ST chipped in a fantasy-relevant 19.0, and Breece Hall carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 18.8. Sir Jo-Nurse read the matchup well enough down the stretch, even if the margin was thin as a granola bar wrapper.

The Machine Knows got 35.66 out of Josh Allen, which on most weeks is a laminated golden ticket, but Rico Dowdle spent Sunday looking like a stunned mule near the goal line, managing only 3.1 on a projection nearly quadruple that. Javonte Williams did his part with 21.7, but the rest of the roster was stuck in the Sewards while Funk that Junk's stars just outpaced them. Boss G12 Member had the horsepower and still watched it idle in the driveway.

Paralegal and Counsel got the backfield of dreams to open the year, with D'Andre Swift and Jahmyr Gibbs combining for over 63 points like they were splitting a hike map between them. A.J. Brown no-showed at 4.1 against an 11.54 projection, but with that kind of Boss running behind him it barely registered. This was a Penis Eating Pike of a week one debut, and the Goose never had an answer.

Chef Boyardee, or however you want to butcher Stefanowitcz this week, got a real Guide Rec out of Jonathan Taylor's 23.6, but everything around him fell apart. Terry McLaurin caught nothing worth mentioning and finished with 2.4 points against a projection near double digits — Stole my wow doesn't begin to cover it. The Goose's game plan never adjusted to the deficit, and 55 Burgers cruised to a post-hike scrub-caliber margin without needing to sweat a single decision.

Team Bradford, still without an ounce of Campcraft Enthusiast subtlety, ran up 108.84 on the back of Derrick Henry's 34.8, who bulldozed his way to the end zone with the kind of ease that makes a defense look like it forgot how tackling works. Bijan Robinson chipped in 27.3 and DJ Moore added 18.5, which meant Bo Nix's 5.44 and Davante Adams' Beak afternoon barely mattered. The game plan was Boss even when the depth chart wasn't.

Love Thy Naber never found a pulse. Flame On watched Matthew Stafford post a Beak 4.1, Jaylen Waddle disappear for 0.7, and the whole operation Had their lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow from kickoff onward. Parker Washington's 16.8 and CeeDee Lamb's 12.9 were the only signs of life in an otherwise stunned outfit, and 58.4 points isn't going to out-coach anybody. Chief Ron Voice: I'm disappointed in you. This was Beak coaching against a Boss game plan, and the scoreboard knew it early.

Week 1 and The Island Gudge already look like they know something the rest of the league doesn't. Kenneth Walker III went off for 32.6, Christian Watson chipped in 29.7, Amon-Ra St. Brown added 23.7, and suddenly a 54-point margin feels less like luck and more like a manager who simply saw the board clearly while everyone else squinted. Quinshon Judkins was the lone flat note at 6.0, but with a haul like that it barely registered.

Ricky Huns got a boss night from Jaxson Dart at 26.6 and Ladd McConkey chipping in 16.7, but 94.9 was never going to survive a Boss Section Chief clinic like this one. The rest of the lineup was on the Point most of the afternoon, and the game plan never found an answer once the Island Gudge started pulling away. A 54.26-point beatdown in Week 1 is the kind of statement win that makes the rest of the league check the schedule twice.

headline: Chase Brown had a bad scare survives Harley Jarvis rally
